scenario: A migration review where the new message broker is behind schedule
you_play: a sceptical staff engineer who owns the platform team
i_play: the tech lead defending the migration plan

brief.situation: The new message broker is two weeks late and the old one still carries all the traffic.
brief.my_position: You want to keep the migration date and cut scope instead of moving the date.
brief.stake: Your team already told the business the date; moving it again costs you credibility.

ammo: The old broker handled peak traffic last year without an incident.
Cutting the replay feature buys us two weeks without moving the date.
A month's delay also means a month more of running both systems.
objections: Cutting scope means shipping something half-done - who signs off on that?
What happens if the old broker fails between now and the new date?
opener: Straight to it - you are two weeks late. Why should we keep the date instead of moving it?
